div.p: Critical real time system must run under high dependable environment which guarantees a high level of reliability and security. Fault tolerance and security technique has played an important role in building such environment. In this paper, we provide an improved technique to schedule such tasks with high reliability and security requirement on high dependable distributed real time system. First, the paper analyzed the scheduling problem on high dependable distributed real time system and provided a refined scheduling model which accurately described processors, fault tolerant tasks and security overhead. Based on the scheduling model, it proposed a new and better scheduling algorithm Security Driven Fault Tolerant Scheduling Algorithm (SDFT) which extended FTRMFF algorithm to tolerate N processors failure at one time, and it introduced a new global scheduler to improve efficiency of scheduling process. Moreover, the SDFT supported flexible security policy applied on real time tasks according to its security requirement and considered the effect of security overhead during scheduling. In addition, the paper adopted and extended the Completion Time Test (CTT) as the schedulability criteria. Simulation experiments showed the SDFT algorithm could achieve better reliability and security at the cost of less number of processors.

div.head: Introduction
div.p: In real time system design, scheduling algorithm has played an important role in keeping system running correctly and efficiently. With the developing of industry and computer science, there is an increasing demand for more reliable and secure design in building high dependence real time system. Traditional scheduling algorithms have paid too much attention to improving the efficiency of scheduling process and neglected the reliability and security requirement of scheduled tasks, which makes it unsuitable to high dependence real time system. Thereby, it's necessary to invent a novel scheduling algorithm which could adopt both fault tolerance and security technique.

Currently, there are many schemes proposed to schedule tasks in real time system. Liu and Layland [2] firstly proposed famous Rate-Monotonic (RM) algorithm which supported preemptively scheduling periodic tasks (which deadline equal to period) only on single processor. Dhal and Liu [3] extended the RM algorithm to Rate Monotonic First-Fit (RMFF) algorithm, which supported scheduling real time tasks on multiprocessor system. Moreover, Alan and Luigi [1] proposed Fault Tolerant RMFF (FFRMFF) algorithm based on RMFF which introduced fault tolerance technique to RMFF, but it didn't consider the security requirement of real time tasks and tolerated only one processor failure. Tao and Qin [4] proposed a novel dynamic scheduling algorithm with security awareness, but the algorithm didn't support static scheduling which made it not be adaptive to scheduling large numbers of periodic tasks, and most importantly, it didn't support fault tolerance.

It is noted that none of the schemes discussed above have both considered the security requirement of real time tasks and achieved fault tolerance. Indeed, the idea seems useful for providing a novel technique to schedule real time tasks with reliability and security guaranteed. The present paper considers the problem of scheduling a set of independent periodic tasks with high reliability and security requirement on high dependable scheduler to improve efficiency of scheduling process. Moreover, the SDFT supported flexible security policy applied on real time tasks which achieved best fit security level according to its security requirement.

The rest of the paper is organized as follows. Section 2 gives a formal definition of the scheduling problem and a precise specification of the fault tolerance task and security overhead model. Section 3 provides a description of the proposed Safety Driven Fault-Tolerant (SDFT) scheduling algorithm. In Section 4, simulation experiments are arranged to check the efficiency of the SDFT algorithm. Finally, Section 5 summarizes the work and discusses further possible extensions..

div.head: Scheduling Problem
div.p: The paper studies a distributed real time system which composed by a set of heterogeneous processors with independent periodic tasks with high security and reliability requirement running on them. The scheduling problem consists of finding a schedule (or order) in which all the periodic requests of the tasks are to be executed on the processors so as to satisfy the following scheduling conditions [1,4] :
(C1) Timeliness requirement are met, namely, each task must be executed completely before its deadline.
(C2) Security requirement are met, namely, each task must apply its security policy when running.
(C3) Reliability requirement are met, namely, each task must be completed correctly despite of the occurrence of processor failure.

div.head: Processor Model
div.p: In high dependable real time system, each task requires a certain level of security which could be concluded three typical security demands: confidentiality, integrity and identifiability. Based on those demands, high dependable system has provided corresponding security services: encryption/decryption, hash function and digital signature.

By assembling these security services in diverse style, system could provide flexible security policies to meet task's specific security requirement. But security policies incur extra overhead including computing and storage usage [6] , thus they would affect scheduling process unavoidablely and couldn't be ignored. So we should analyze the security overhead accurately so as to estimate the correct effects on every task. The results of two experiments are shown in Fig. 2. The ratio of ( ) ( )/ ( ) N SDFT N RMFF N RMFF denotes the excess number of processor required by SDFF. The bigger ratio reveals more processor required. In the left figure of Fig. 2, SDFF needs more processor when redundancy R increases. It's noting that the increase of ( ) ( )/ ( ) N SDFT N RMFF N RMFF isn't proportional to R which prove that SDFT requires less processors to provide fault tolerance. In the right figure of Fig. 2,( ) ( )/ ( ) N SDFT N RMFF N RMFF increases with security cost SC , it reveals that the higher security cost could downgrade the performance of scheduling process greatly. Thereby, we must design better security policy to make a balance between high schedulability and high security in practice.

In the newest experiment, we compare the SDFT algorithm with the FTRMFF by running them under the same task sets produced by random. From the final result we conclude that SDFT gets the same performance with FTRMFF when 1 R , but SDFT need more processors to support higher redundancy when R increases in the latter test. In addition, FTRMFF cannot provide a schedule when the security overhead increases to some value because it neglects the effect of security overhead to scheduler, but SDFT can produce a feasible schedule to afford the security cost.

div.head: Conclusions
div.p: This paper has taken the problem of scheduling a set of independent periodic tasks on heterogeneous processor into account. The proposed SDFT algorithm extends RMFF scheduling algorithm to both tolerate more failures and support flexible security policy. Simulation experiments showed the SDFT algorithm can achieve better reliability and security at the cost of less number of processors. Further research would focus on these fields such as considering message communication overhead, the relevant relationship of tasks, and extending SDFT algorithm to meet safety requirement, and so on.
